title: Composition of derived pro-etale module pullbacks
statement:
Let $h:Z\to W$ and $k:W\to V$ be morphisms of schemes, with small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and inverse images $h^{-1},k^{-1},(kh)^{-1}$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Let $R_V,R_W,R_Z$ be sheaves of commutative rings on $V_{\mathrm{proet}},W_{\mathrm{proet}},Z_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with identifications $k^{-1}R_V\cong R_W$ and $h^{-1}R_W\cong R_Z$, and give $(kh)^{-1}R_V$ the identification with $R_Z$ obtained through the canonical isomorphism $(kh)^{-1}\cong h^{-1}k^{-1}$. With the derived module pullbacks $Lh^*,Lk^*,L(kh)^*$ of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] there is a canonical isomorphism of functors

$$
 c_{h,k}:L(k\circ h)^*\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Lh^*\circ Lk^*:\ D(V_{\mathrm{proet}},R_V)\longrightarrow D(Z_{\mathrm{proet}},R_Z),
$$

which on a K-flat complex $\mathcal K^\bullet$ of $R_V$-modules with flat terms is the class of the termwise canonical isomorphism of module pullbacks $(kh)^*\mathcal K^\bullet\cong h^*k^*\mathcal K^\bullet$ (here $k^*\mathcal K^\bullet$ is again K-flat with flat terms, so it computes $Lk^*$ and $h^*k^*\mathcal K^\bullet$ computes $Lh^*Lk^*$).

proof.text: Choose the canonical module adjunctions supplied by def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations. Their existsUnique normalization theorem, evaluated at the identity map and then at the model pullback unit, proves the required sectionwise tensor-unit normalization. Apply lem-sf-proetale-tensor-composition-unit to obtain the module direct-image pasting isomorphism. Invert it; its section formula follows by applying restriction along the inverse pasting map to its given section equation and cancelling the two inverse maps. Define a as its inverse image under conjugateIsoEquiv for the composite and single module adjunctions. The equivalence inverse identity proves the conjugation equation.

Apply NatIso.mapHomologicalComplex to a and the canonical comparison for the composite of additive functors to obtain b; its degree component is exactly a. The exact module pullbacks have the published derived factorization isomorphisms on every complex. Descend a with Functor.mapDerivedCategoryNatIso, then compose with Functor.mapDerivedCategoryCompIso. These proved source-library APIs implement the quasi-isomorphism localization universal property. The equations mapDerivedCategoryNatIso_fac and mapDerivedCategoryCompIso_hom_app_factors give the required representative formula on every complex. The termwise map of a agrees with b by homological-complex extensionality, so no resolution choice is needed.

Apply lem-sp-proetale-algebraic-inverse-image to k and R_V. Its module-functor equality identifies the existing pullback object and map formulas with the tensor extension of that algebraic inverse image. The finite-limit preservation clause of det-pe-topos-functoriality-inverse-image supplies the geometric-morphism hypothesis on the specified set inverse image. Apply lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat with these formulas and c_k.hom. It gives K-flatness and flatness of all terms of the pulled-back complex. Combine these two conclusions with the localization equation from the preceding step. The argument does not choose a K-flat resolution: exact termwise descent already supplies the comparison on every complex.
